previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for evaluation of diarrhea, weight loss, and malaise. She was found to have severe neutropenia, acute kidney injury, and non-gap metabolic acidosis. Infectious workup including stool, blood, and urine cultures was negative, and CMV viral load was undetectable. An EGD and colonoscopy revealed histologic evidence of ischemic colitis, likely due to mycophenolate mofetil, prompting a switch to myfortic with rapid improvement in diarrhea. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted to improve low white blood cell counts, and tacrolimus was uptitrated to 3 mg twice daily. She was started on megace for appetite stimulation and zinc for deficiency, leading to weight gain from 50.8 kg to 54.9 kg. Her kidney function improved with hydration, and she was discharged on stable medications with plans for close outpatient follow-up, including weekly CMV monitoring and transplant clinic visit.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with HCV cirrhosis, HCC, s/p OLT c/b moderate acute cellular 
rejection from tacrolimus noncompliance, recurrent HCV, now 
cured, portal hypertension, ascites, HE, CKD III, recent 
admission for diarrhea, malnutrition, neutropenia, and ___, 
presents several days after discharge for acute on chronic 
kidney injury.

# Acute on chronic kidney injury. Discharged with Cr 1.5, with 
increase to 2.1 a few days later with K 5.3 at PCP visit, 
thought likely pre renal from poor PO intake and diarrhea. No 
report of hypotension. There was thought to be a possible 
contribution form Bactrim use as well that had been restarted on 
last admission. Bactrim was discontinued. Creatinine improved 
with IV albumin, improved diarrhea, and increased PO intake 
while in the hospital. Cr of 1.3 on discharge. 

# Diarrhea: Patient with continued report of very loose bowel 
movements. Previous admission with evidence of colitis 
concerning for possible MMF side effect and transitioned to 
myfortic. Had been improving prior to discharge with resolution 
of diarrhea on myfortic, though appeared to have re occurrence 
of diarrhea while on myfortic. Stool studies were sent and were 
negative for infection. Myfortic was held completely on 
discharge given concern for severity of diarrhea.

# Pancytopenia/Severe Neutropenia: Has been a continued problem 
since prior admission, thought to be a medication effect from 
multiple immunosuppressants. There was no evidence of infection. 
As above, bactrim and myfortic were stopped during the 
admission. CMV VL was negative; to be checked weekly as valcyte 
also discontinued on previous admission. ___ improved to 996 on 
discharge with these medication changes. The patient will have 
close follow up with at least weekly lab testing. 

# OLT c/b recurrent HCV Cirrhosis: HCV cirrhosis and HCC s/p 
transplant complicated by moderate acute cellular rejection in 
the setting of brief tacrolimus noncompliance, recurrent 
hepatitis C now cured and cirrhosis complicated by portal 
hypertension, ascites, and hepatic encephalopathy. With stable 
but elevated LFTS in setting of downtitration of 
immunosuppression. Biopsy deferred on previous admission. The 
patient was continued on prednisone 10 mg daily and tacrolimus 3 
mg  Q12H. As above. myfortic was discontinued. The palliative 
care was consulted to help clarify the patient's goals of care 
given her frustration with continued hospitalizations. She 
clearly stated that she would want to return to the hospital  in 
spite of this, and she would let her PCP (who was also 
functioning as the ___ know of this 
change). The patient was amenable to ___ care for blood draws. 

=====================
CHRONIC ISSUES
=====================
# Non-gap acidosis. Likely from AoCKD, recent diarrhea. The 
patient was continued on PO bicarbonate. 

# Hepatic encephalopathy: History of hepatic encephalopathy post 

transplant. There was no evidence of hepatic encephalopathy 
during the admission. The patient has a known tremor that is not 
asterixis. Continued on lactulose and rifaximin.

# GIB/Varices: Last EGD with 2 cords of grade I varices. The 
patient was continued on carvedilol.

# Severe malnutrition: Started on megace during lass admission, 
and mirtazapine had been held due to concern for contribution to 
somnolence. The patient completed a 14 dy course of zince. 
Continued on nepro TID with meals. 

# Type II Diabetes: Blood sugars somewhat labile with episodes 
of hyperglycemia but also blood sugars <100. Thought secondary 
to megace initiation on previous admission. Insulin regimen 
uptitrated on prior admission. No changes made during this 
admission given overall stability and concern for hypoglycemia. 

# Hypertension: Stable. Patient continued carvedilol and 
amlodipine. 

# Osteopenia/Bone Health: Patient continued vitamin D and 
calcium. 

# Glaucoma: Patient conitnued home latanoprost and timolol. 

# History of Seizure: Patient continued keppra.  

# Essential Tremor: Patient continued primidone.
